# Rummage

> A hide-and-seek game in the browser where every drawer, door and lid really opens. All 55 pieces of furniture were generated by Aholo Lux3D text-to-3D and articulated by Lux3D (107 working joints, read from Lux3D's URDF output). Built for the Manycore Aholo Global 3D AI Hackathon, November 2026.

- Play: https://rummage-game.vercel.app (no login, desktop or phone, English and Simplified Chinese)
- ModelScope Studio: https://www.modelscope.ai/studios/heisemma/rummage
- Source, judges' guide and live checks: https://github.com/emmaGH1/rummage (README.md, JUDGES.md, `node scripts/check-live.mjs`)

## How Lux3D is used
- One sentence per piece → Lux3D text-to-3D (G1-Turbo, cartoon style), median 117 s.
- A one-line motion prompt → Lux3D articulation, which returns robot.urdf plus one GLB per moving part, median 154 s.
- The game loads each URDF with three.js and urdf-loader; every joint (60 revolute, 47 prismatic) is a hiding spot.
- Per-piece prompts, motion prompts, joints and timings: https://rummage-game.vercel.app/lux3d-manifest.json
- Shipped Lux3D output: https://rummage-game.vercel.app/models/<piece>/robot.urdf and /models/<piece>/meshes/*.glb

## The game
- 10 levels: five rooms by day, then by night with a flashlight. Mechanics: decoys, padlocks with a brass key, mimics that bite, riddles, clue hints, risky bets, a reveal of missed keys.
- Challenge a friend: hide a key and share a link (no server; the challenge is in the URL).
- Keys are placed fairly at random every run; no spot holds a key in more than 25% of runs.
